name: OpenAI, Inc.
jurisdiction: Delaware (registered as charitable trust in California)
short: The original 501(c)(3). Plaintiffs allege its assets, IP, and personnel were transferred into the for-profit layers; defense says the nonprofit retains supervisory and economic interests.
description: Filed in Delaware as a nonprofit corporation; registered with the California Attorney General's Registry of Charitable Trusts in August 2017. Certificate of incorporation states OpenAI 'shall be a nonprofit corporation organized exclusively for charitable and/or educational purposes within the meaning of section 501(c)(3).' The board of OpenAI, Inc. — not the LP — is the entity to which Musk's donations flowed. Site of the November 2023 board crisis. Day 7 Wu deposition testimony added that the nonprofit residual sits behind roughly $250B in aggregate target redemptions and that OpenAI Inc. has no full-time employees apart from board / CEO structure.

flows.detail: $44.56M wired 2016–2020 per FAC ¶424; ~$38M cash on Birchall's trial chart

Plaintiffs allege exclusive licensing arrangement transferred IP control to the for-profit layer; Wu testified OpenAI Inc. transferred developed IP and most employees to the for-profit LP / OpCo structure
Wu described roughly $250B in aggregate target redemptions across LPs before the nonprofit residual would be paid

attributes: 'Organized exclusively for charitable and/or educational purposes'
Funds and assets diverted into for-profit subsidiaries
No full-time employees; nonprofit residual behind roughly $250B aggregate target redemptions before payout

name: OpenAI, L.P.
short: Capped-profit LP launched March 2019 as a for-profit subsidiary of OpenAI, Inc. Designed with 'fixed maximum return' caps for investors. Renamed/restructured into OpenAI OpCo, LLC.
description: Created as the vehicle for outside capital after the 2018–2019 strategic pivot. Microsoft's 2019 $1B and 2023 $10B investments flowed here. Plaintiffs allege the 'profit cap' was effectively removed in the 2024–2025 restructuring; defense disputes the framing of the restructuring. Wu's Day 7 30(b)(6) deposition put trial numbers on the waterfall: Microsoft's 2019 $1B round carried a $20B target redemption, the 2023 $10B round carried a $60B / 6x target, and aggregate target redemptions were roughly $250B before the nonprofit residual.

flows.detail: Reported $13.75B cumulative through 2024; Wu testified the 2019 $1B Microsoft investment carried a $20B target redemption and the 2023 $10B commitment carried a $60B target redemption
Target-redemption stack described as roughly $250B, with a 20% annual escalator starting in 2025

attributes: Microsoft 2019: $20B target on $1B; Microsoft 2023: $60B target on $10B; aggregate LP stack roughly $250B before nonprofit residual

name: OpenAI OpCo, LLC
short: Successor name for the operating for-profit. Named defendant in every iteration of the complaint.
description: Houses commercial activities and exclusive licensing arrangements with Microsoft; site of the 2024–2025 restructuring at issue. Wu's Day 7 testimony said the 2023 second amended JDCA licensed Microsoft all OpenAI IP and technology except AGI, while the non-binding Watershed MOU would give Microsoft certain product-IP access after a third-party AGI determination.

name: OpenAI GP, L.L.C.
short: General partner of OpenAI, L.P. Management entity for the for-profit layer.
description: Plaintiffs say the GP layer is where management and control rights reside; named defendant on every iteration.

name: OpenAI, L.L.C.
short: Intermediate holding/management entity in the OpenAI corporate web.

name: OpenAI Global, LLC
short: Global commercial-business vehicle within the for-profit layer.

name: OpenAI Holdings, LLC
short: Equity/assets holding structure within the for-profit corporate web.

name: OAI Corporation, LLC
short: Supplementary operational/holding entity named in every complaint caption.

name: OpenAI Startup Fund Management, LLC
short: Manages OpenAI's downstream startup investment program. Plaintiffs say this is where the alleged 'fund-no-competitors' covenant operates.

name: OpenAI Startup Fund I, L.P.
short: Limited partnership raising outside capital; plaintiffs allege LP agreements include no-compete-with-OpenAI commitments. The court found xAI 'could not provide a single declaration from an investor to confirm its theory'.

name: OpenAI Startup Fund GP I, L.L.C.
short: Manages the Startup Fund I LP; participates in deal selection and capital deployment.

name: OpenAI Startup Fund SPV GP I-IV, L.L.C.
short: Four GPs for the SPV layer.

name: OpenAI Startup Fund SPV I-IV, L.P.
short: Four downstream SPV limited partnerships. Plaintiffs say the SPV layer obscures beneficial ownership of for-profit interests.

name: Aestas Management Company, LLC
short: Named defendant in original complaint and SAC. Holds/manages stakes in for-profit entities; alleged in SAC to be a control vehicle for insiders.
description: Per FAC ¶551–559, formed 2023 as a general operating partner for parts of the for-profit network. Plaintiffs add Aestas back as a named defendant in the SAC.

name: Aestas, LLC
short: Sister Aestas entity, predating the management company. Plaintiffs allege it holds for-profit interests.

name: Microsoft Corp.
short: Investor, exclusive cloud provider, and licensee. After MSJ, the remaining Microsoft claim is aiding and abetting breach of fiduciary duty.
description: Microsoft's MSJ characterizes the relationship as 'arm's-length negotiations between sophisticated parties'; it 'did not receive a conventional equity ownership interest' but a capped-return arrangement. Plaintiffs cite Microsoft's 2019 $1B, 2023 $10B, and 2024 expanded investments and the November 2023 board episode as evidence Microsoft exerts de facto control. Day 7 Wu deposition testimony added that Microsoft's 2023 round had a $60B / 6x target redemption, that the 2023 JDCA licensed Microsoft all IP and technology except AGI, and that the Watershed MOU would provide certain post-AGI product-IP access after a third-party-panel determination.

flows.detail: $1B (2019) with $20B target redemption → $10B (2023) with $60B / 6x target redemption → expanded 2024
Exclusive cloud relationship; below-cost pricing alleged by plaintiffs (rejected at PI stage)
2023 second amended JDCA licensed all OpenAI IP and technology except AGI; Watershed MOU would provide certain product-IP access after AGI determination

name: X.AI Corp.
short: Musk's competing AI company. Co-plaintiff on antitrust and unfair-competition counts in the FAC (Nov 2024) and SAC (May 2025).
description: Trial-record evidence showed xAI raised over $11 billion (Dkt #121 p.8). xAI converted from a public benefit corporation to a C-corp during 2025; on cross, Musk testified 'a B-corp and a C-corp are pretty much the same thing' (043026TT.txt:1838). xAI has no profit caps for its investors (043026TT.txt:1997).

name: Tesla, Inc.
short: Not a party. Featured because Musk proposed in 2018 that OpenAI 'attach to Tesla as its cash cow' (DX 749) and because Tesla has parallel AI/robotics ambitions ('AI-enabled robot army', 042926TT.txt:4814).

name: Neuralink Corp.
short: Not a party. Featured via the October 2017 Musk email to Ben Rapoport: 'I have no problem if you pitch people at OpenAI to work at Neuralink' (DX 719) — used by defense to show Musk's view of cross-company recruitment.

name: Musk Foundation
short: Musk's family foundation; CFO Birchall managed donations. Some of Musk's contributions to OpenAI were routed through donor-advised funds (DAFs) and YC.org as fiscal sponsor — the basis of OpenAI's 'no settlor standing' argument.

name: YC.org
short: Acted as fiscal sponsor for early OpenAI contributions. Plaintiffs cite YC.org's role to argue Musk's donations were directed to OpenAI; defense argues the indirect path defeats settlor standing.

name: Musk Industries (Excession LLC)
short: Musk's personal family office. Per FAC ¶425, paid OpenAI's monthly office rent and overhead; on the lease for the Pioneer Building. DX 600 (Birchall to Sam Teller, Jan 2017): 'Elon holds 100 percent of the power and authority regarding the building.'
